_about: Edition-2 occurrence-level QAC 0.4 corrections, adjudicated from the vocalised Uthmani word, governing particles and verse i'rab (heuristic screens check_verbs.py and check_cases.py; adjudication inputs/results in reports/adjudication/). Raw metadata stays unchanged; same format as content-pipeline/meta/overrides.json, plus optional aspect (PERF/IMPF) for mis-tagged aspect.

4:3:28.noteEnglish: QAC tags تَعُولُوا۟ jussive, but أَلَّا is أَنْ (masdariyya, nasb particle) + negative لَا; the dropped nun is the sign of nasb, and the ayah note itself treats «ألا تعولوا» as an interpreted masdar: subjunctive.

4:12:22.noteEnglish: QAC gives يُوصِينَ the pseudo-lemma yuwSiy as Form I; the active prefix vowel u with kasra before the final radical is the Form IV imperfect of أَوْصَى (as يُوصِيكُمُ 4:11 and يُوصِى 4:11). Active, mabni on sukun with the feminine nun as subject.

4:42:8.noteEnglish: QAC gives تُسَوَّىٰ the pseudo-lemma tusaw~aY` as Form I; the doubled waw (shadda) makes it the Form II passive of سَوَّى (Form I passive would be تُسْوَى). Indicative with implied damma after لَوْ, ٱلْأَرْضُ its na'ib al-fa'il.

4:43:33.noteEnglish: QAC tags لَـٰمَسْتُمُ as Form I; the vocalised Hafs word belongs to لَامَسَ (Form III), as decided and double-reviewed in the edition-2 verb-paradigm library entry (lamasu|I|ACT). The lexeme handle is kept; follow the reviewed paradigm.

4:49:13.noteEnglish: QAC tags يُظْلَمُونَ jussive (and the generated i'rab line repeats مجزوم), but the retained nun of the five verbs shows it is indicative; لَا here is plain negation of a third-person passive statement, not prohibition (which would drop the nun). The verse note coordinates وَلَا يُظْلَمُونَ as a statement with بَلِ ٱللَّهُ يُزَكِّى.

4:61:4.noteEnglish: QAC tags تَعَالَوْا۟ as Form IV; the vocalised Hafs word belongs to تَعَالَى (Form VI), as decided and double-reviewed in the edition-2 verb-paradigm library entry (taEaAla|IV|ACT). The lexeme handle is kept; follow the reviewed paradigm.

4:64:6.noteEnglish: QAC tags لِيُطَاعَ as Form I; the vocalised Hafs word belongs to أُطِيعَ (Form IV), as decided and double-reviewed in the edition-2 verb-paradigm library entry (yuTaAEu|I|PASS). The lexeme handle is kept; follow the reviewed paradigm.

4:77:47.noteEnglish: QAC tags تُظْلَمُونَ jussive (and the generated i'rab line repeats مجزوم), but the retained nun shows it is indicative; وَلَا is negation in a promise (injustice will not be done to you), not prohibition, which would read تُظْلَمُوا۟. The verse note coordinates it with the nominal sentence وَٱلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ.

4:103:11.noteEnglish: QAC tags ٱطْمَأْنَنتُمْ as Form XII; the vocalised Hafs word belongs to اِطْمَأَنَّ (Form QIV), as decided and double-reviewed in the edition-2 verb-paradigm library entry ({Toma>an~a|XII|ACT). The lexeme handle is kept; follow the reviewed paradigm.

4:105:10.noteEnglish: QAC tags أَرَىٰكَ a 1st-person singular subjunctive imperfect, but in بِمَآ أَرَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ the nominative ٱللَّهُ is its subject and no particle of nasb precedes it: it is the Form IV perfect أَرَى (He showed you), 3rd masculine singular, in the relative clause of مَا. The generated i'rab line 'مضارع منصوب' follows the faulty tag.

4:108:14.noteEnglish: QAC tags يَرْضَىٰ subjunctive, but in مَا لَا يَرْضَىٰ the لَا is plain negation inside a relative clause and nothing governs nasb; it is indicative with an implied damma on the alif maqsura.

4:115:6.noteEnglish: QAC labels mā relative. The verse i‘rab explicitly treats it as a masdar particle. The interpreted masdar is the genitive complement of the preceding adverb.

4:124:15.noteEnglish: QAC tags يُظْلَمُونَ jussive, but its nun is retained (sign of raf') after negative لَا; it is joined to the nominal answer فَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ يَدْخُلُونَ, which is not in jazm, so it is indicative.

4:127:9.noteEnglish: QAC tags يُتْلَىٰ subjunctive, but in وَمَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ the مَا is relative and no particle of nasb precedes; it is an indicative passive with an implied damma on the alif maqsura.

4:140:11.noteEnglish: QAC omits PASS, but يُكْفَرُ has prefix-u with fatha on the fa (active Form I would be يَكْفُرُ): it is the Form I passive (they are disbelieved in), with بِهَا as na'ib al-fa'il, parallel to the passive وَيُسْتَهْزَأُ بِهَا.

4:171:4.noteEnglish: QAC 0.4 tags لَا تَغْلُوا۟ 2nd person dual (the generated i'rab calls the suffix الألف), but it addresses يَـٰٓأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبِ (cf. دِينِكُمْ) and the Uthmani unpronounced ا۟ is alif al-fariqa after wāw al-jamā'a: 2MP jussive after prohibitive لَا, nun deleted, the wāw is the subject.

7:16:2.noteEnglish: QAC tags the mā of فَبِمَآ relative. The verse i‘rab explicitly reads it as a masdar particle after causal bāʾ. The interpreted masdar is genitive and attaches to the ensuing verb of ambush.

7:17:2.noteEnglish: QAC tags لَـَٔاتِيَنَّهُم 2nd person masculine singular, but its prefix is hamza (أَ), the 1st person singular marker: Iblis says 'I will surely come to them'. Its mood stays as tagged: the fatha comes from the energetic nun of the oath answer (mabni), not from subjunctive nasb.

7:20:1.noteEnglish: QAC tags فَوَسْوَسَ as Form I; the vocalised Hafs word belongs to وَسْوَسَ (Form QI), as decided and double-reviewed in the edition-2 verb-paradigm library entry (wasowasa|I|ACT). The lexeme handle is kept; follow the reviewed paradigm.

7:22:1.noteEnglish: QAC tags فَدَلَّىٰهُمَا as Form I; the vocalised Hafs word belongs to دَلَّى (Form II), as decided and double-reviewed in the edition-2 verb-paradigm library entry (dal~a|I|ACT). The lexeme handle is kept; follow the reviewed paradigm.

7:27:14.noteEnglish: QAC tags لِيُرِيَهُمَا passive. The vocalized يُرِيَ is active Form IV of أَرَى, subjunctive after purpose lām. The subject refers to Satan, the dual pronoun is the first object, and the following noun is the second object. Use the active paradigm.

7:35:18.noteEnglish: QAC groups this occurrence under the transitive lemma حَزَنَ يَحْزُنُ. The fatḥa on zāy and the intransitive sense of feeling sorrow establish حَزِنَ يَحْزَنُ (Form I, samiʿa class). Preserve the occurrence mood and person.

7:38:21.noteEnglish: QAC tags ٱدَّارَكُوا۟ as a second-person plural imperative. It follows حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا and describes successive groups entering together. It is a third-person masculine plural perfect of assimilated Form VI, as recognized by the supplied paradigm.

7:48:9.noteEnglish: QAC tags أَغْنَىٰ as Form I; the vocalised Hafs word belongs to أَغْنَى (Form IV), as decided and double-reviewed in the edition-2 verb-paradigm library entry (>agonaY`|I|ACT). The lexeme handle is kept; follow the reviewed paradigm.

7:48:12.noteEnglish: QAC tags the mā in وَمَا as relative. The verse i‘rab makes it a masdar particle and coordinates the interpreted masdar with the preceding subject of أَغْنَى. The lesson follows that reading.

7:49:15.noteEnglish: QAC groups this occurrence under the transitive lemma حَزَنَ يَحْزُنُ. The fatḥa on zāy and the intransitive sense of feeling sorrow establish حَزِنَ يَحْزَنُ (Form I, samiʿa class). Preserve the occurrence mood and person.

7:51:16.noteEnglish: QAC tags the mā in وَمَا as relative. The verse i‘rab treats it as a masdar particle and coordinates the interpreted masdar with the preceding interpreted masdar after the kāf. The lesson follows the verse analysis.

7:92:6.noteEnglish: The inherited override wrongly assigned أَغْنَى Form IV. The open nūn in يَغْنَوْا۟, the intransitive construction with فِيهَا and the sense of dwelling support غَنِيَ يَغْنَى Form I. QAC correctly tags Form I but gives the wrong lemma handle. The preceding لَمْ makes this plural jussive with omitted nūn.

7:143:25.noteEnglish: QAC tags تَجَلَّىٰ as Form I, but the ta- prefix and doubled middle radical (tafaʿʿala) make it Form V of ج ل و (the Form I verb is جَلَا يَجْلُو). The reviewed paradigm entry under this lexeme handle is written as Form V; raised by the lex-a02 library review.

7:163:25.noteEnglish: The verse i‘rab reads the mā after bāʾ as a masdar particle. The interpreted masdar is genitive and depends on the verb of testing. QAC tags the raw segment as relative.

7:189:13.noteEnglish: QAC 0.4 tags تَغَشَّىٰهَا as a 3MS imperfect (indicative by default), but it follows فَلَمَّا and a 3MS imperfect of Form V would be يَتَغَشَّىٰ: it is the Form V perfect taghashshā (3MS, active, no mood), with هَا as object. It is not jussive; treat it as a perfect verb (aspect PERF).

7:190:2.noteEnglish: QAC 0.4 tags ءَاتَىٰهُمَا as a 1st person singular imperfect, but after فَلَمَّا it is the Form IV perfect ātā (aspect PERF, no mood) with Allah as its hidden 3MS subject: 'He gave them'; هُمَا is the first object and صَـٰلِحًا the second.

7:190:8.noteEnglish: QAC 0.4 tags ءَاتَىٰهُمَا as a 1st person singular imperfect, but in فِيمَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمَا it is the Form IV perfect ātā (aspect PERF, no mood) in the relative clause, with Allah as hidden 3MS subject: 'what He gave them'.

7:190:9.noteEnglish: QAC tags فَتَعَـٰلَى as Form I; the vocalised Hafs word belongs to تَعَالَى (Form VI), as decided and double-reviewed in the edition-2 verb-paradigm library entry (taEa`laY`|I|ACT). The lexeme handle is kept; follow the reviewed paradigm.

7:203:12.noteEnglish: QAC tags يُوحَىٰٓ subjunctive, but no particle of nasb precedes it (it is the verb of the relative clause after مَا); it is indicative with an implied damma on the alif (للتعذر), passive Form IV.

25:17:11.noteEnglish: QAC tags عِبَادِى nominative, but in ءَأَنتُمْ أَضْلَلْتُمْ عِبَادِى it is the direct object of أَضْلَلْتُمْ (whose subject is the تُمْ suffix): accusative with the fatha implied before the 1S ya, هَـٰٓؤُلَآءِ following as its descriptor.

25:30:5.noteEnglish: QAC tags قَوْمِى nominative, but in إِنَّ قَوْمِى ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ it is the noun (ism) of إِنَّ: accusative with the fatha implied before the 1S ya; the predicate is the clause ٱتَّخَذُوا۟.

25:45:2.noteEnglish: QAC tags تَرَ 3rd person feminine singular; in أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ it addresses the Prophet (رَبِّكَ), so it is 2nd person masculine singular. The jussive after لَمْ (final alif dropped) is correct.

25:52:2.noteEnglish: QAC tags تُطِعِ third person feminine singular. The paired singular imperatives address the Prophet, so this is second person masculine singular after prohibitive lā. Its final kasra is for joining to the next word.

25:53:4.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ is the object of مَرَجَ (He released the two seas); the dual ya ending marks the accusative.

25:59:3.noteEnglish: QAC tags ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ genitive. It is an object of خَلَقَ and takes kasra in the accusative because it is a sound feminine plural.

25:60:10.noteEnglish: QAC tags mā in لِمَا as relative. The verse i‘rab takes the lām as causal and mā as a masdar particle, with a relative reading possible as an alternative. The lesson follows the verse i‘rab.

29:8:15.noteEnglish: QAC tags تُطِعْهُمَآ third person feminine singular. The nearby singular addressee and the instruction to the person whose parents exert pressure require second person masculine singular, jussive after prohibitive lā.

29:9:4.noteEnglish: QAC tags ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ genitive. The word is the direct object of عَمِلُوا and takes accusative kasra as a sound feminine plural.

29:18:2.noteEnglish: QAC tags تُكَذِّبُوا۟ passive subjunctive. The kasra on the dhal makes it the active Form II (the passive would be تُكَذَّبُوا with fatha), with the waw as subject (if you deny); it is the jussive verb of the conditional وَإِن, its nun dropped for jazm, answered by فَقَدْ كَذَّبَ.

29:30:2.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. رَبِّ (يا محذوفة): an annexed vocative (منادیٰ مضاف) is accusative; the visible kasra signals the first-person ya, so the nasb is implied.

29:33:15.noteEnglish: QAC groups this occurrence under the transitive lemma حَزَنَ يَحْزُنُ. The fatḥa on zāy and the intransitive sense of feeling sorrow establish حَزِنَ يَحْزَنُ (Form I, samiʿa class). Preserve the occurrence mood and person.

29:36:6.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. يَـٰقَوْمِ: an annexed vocative (منادیٰ مضاف) is accusative; the visible kasra signals the first-person ya, so the nasb is implied.

29:48:3.noteEnglish: QAC tags تَتْلُوا۟ 3rd person feminine singular, but its subject is the addressee of وَمَا كُنتَ (you did not recite), parallel to وَلَا تَخُطُّهُۥ; the ta prefix is second person masculine singular. Its indicative mood (khabar of كان, damma implied on the waw; the final alif is orthographic) is correct.

29:51:7.noteEnglish: QAC tags يُتْلَىٰ subjunctive, but no particle of nasb precedes it; it is an indicative passive verbal sentence (hal of ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ per the verse i'rab) with an implied damma.

29:56:1.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. يَـٰعِبَادِىَ: an annexed vocative (منادیٰ مضاف) is accusative; the kasra before the first-person ya means the nasb is implied.

29:56:5.noteEnglish: QAC tags أَرْضِى nominative, but in إِنَّ أَرْضِى وَٰسِعَةٌ it is the noun (ism) of إِنَّ, with وَٰسِعَةٌ as its predicate: accusative, the nasb implied before the first-person ya (the generated i'rab line's مرفوع is wrong here).

91:10:4.noteEnglish: QAC tags دَسَّىٰهَا as Form I; the vocalised Hafs word belongs to دَسَّى (Form II), as decided and double-reviewed in the edition-2 verb-paradigm library entry (das~aY`|I|ACT). The lexeme handle is kept; follow the reviewed paradigm.

91:14:3.noteEnglish: QAC tags فَدَمْدَمَ as Form I; the vocalised Hafs word belongs to دَمْدَمَ (Form QI), as decided and double-reviewed in the edition-2 verb-paradigm library entry (damodama|I|ACT). The lexeme handle is kept; follow the reviewed paradigm.

92:2:3.noteEnglish: QAC tags تَجَلَّىٰ as Form I, but the ta- prefix and doubled middle radical (tafaʿʿala) make it Form V of ج ل و (the Form I verb is جَلَا يَجْلُو). The reviewed paradigm entry under this lexeme handle is written as Form V; raised by the lex-a02 library review.

92:14:3.noteEnglish: QAC gives تَلَظَّىٰ no form tag (Form I); it is Form V تَلَظَّى (tafaʿʿala, ta prefix + doubled middle radical) with one of the two ta's elided from تَتَلَظَّى. Its mood is correctly indicative (hidden damma on the alif; nothing governs it), the sentence being an adjective of نَارًا.

93:8:3.noteEnglish: QAC tags فَأَغْنَىٰ as Form I; the vocalised Hafs word belongs to أَغْنَى (Form IV), as decided and double-reviewed in the edition-2 verb-paradigm library entry (>agonaY`|I|ACT). The lexeme handle is kept; follow the reviewed paradigm.

98:4:9.noteEnglish: The verse i‘rab explicitly reads mā as a masdar particle. The interpreted masdar is the complement of بَعْد, rather than the nominal relative in the raw word tag.

99:1:2.noteEnglish: QAC tags زُلْزِلَتِ as Form I; the vocalised Hafs word belongs to زُلْزِلَ (Form QI), as decided and double-reviewed in the edition-2 verb-paradigm library entry (zulozilu|I|PASS). The lexeme handle is kept; follow the reviewed paradigm.

100:9:4.noteEnglish: QAC tags بُعْثِرَ as Form I; the vocalised Hafs word belongs to بُعْثِرَ (Form QI), as decided and double-reviewed in the edition-2 verb-paradigm library entry (buEovira|I|PASS). The lexeme handle is kept; follow the reviewed paradigm.
